iterations.notes: All six rules checked. R1: every hill afternoon ends with the sun an hour from leaving the sky. R2: no Mr. Pike, no gate. R3: the kitchen goes dark, Leo cannot see his own feet, he lights the torch and names Captain Crunch aloud — something he found himself — so both clauses are met; the critic noted the darkness is incidental rather than entered, and read the rule as written for deliberate entry. R4: no fence or gate is crossed on the page, so the rule is not engaged. R5: Leo has not reached the other side. R6: nothing brightens the torch, no replacement is offered, and nothing measures what is left — the critic checked the 'old batteries that had once belonged to something else' in the drawer and found they are never connected to the torch.
iterations.orchestrator_note: Arbitration on R3: the critic's reading is accepted. R3 was rewritten before FLOW-4 precisely so it would have one reading, and 'enters a space dark enough that he cannot see his own feet' is what the scene does — the lights go out around him and he performs both clauses before moving. The spare batteries in the drawer were watched closely because R6 forbids a replacement; they are scenery in a drawer and the torch is never given one.
